sections.what: No library item declares which biomes or area tags it belongs in. A repo-wide grep of data/library/items/ for the wilderness biome tags (forest, woods, rocky, farmland, shore, ruin, road, dense) returns ZERO matches, so engine/population.py:120-121 tag-intersects to nothing and every compiled wilderness area plans empty (routes/population_ops.py returns status empty). The only bridges today are storage/trade/religious, all from building biomes. Add an affinity/habitat field to the item schema (routes/library_ops.py:118-141) and backfill the wilderness vocabulary. This is the vocabulary bridge that task-569 and task-570 both need.
sections.why: Wilderness area planning matched zero items because wilderness tags did not intersect with item general tags. Adding an explicit affinity list to item schemas and population indexing allows natural resource distribution into wilderness biomes without polluting item role tags.
sections.how:
Added optional affinity list on the item schema in engine/library_nodes.py, threaded through 
routes/library_ops.py and 
routes/graph_ops.py. Updated engine/population.py to union affinity and tags when indexing domains for area population. Authored tools/backfill_item_affinity.py deriving affinities for 361 raw natural resource item templates from their existing tags.
sections.verify:
1. Run population tests targeting item affinity
   - expected: pytest tests/test_population.py passes all tests including affinity matching
   - observed: 5 passed in tests/test_population.py
2. Verify backfill script stability
   - expected: python tools/backfill_item_affinity.py --check reports zero missing affinities
   - observed: 361 natural resource items verified

acceptance.text: Item schema accepts optional affinity array of biome tags.
engine/population.py considers affinity when matching items to areas.
Wilderness natural resources (herbs, ore, wood, fish, berries) carry appropriate wilderness affinity tags.
Population planner populates wilderness cells from matching affinity pool.
